answer: Forging thousands of identities then costs the attacker a full bond per fake agent plus slashing risk, making it a gale of expense rather than a breeze. Sybil resistance via stake-weighted identity binding: each agent must lock a bonded stake to register, and reputation accrues along a single cryptographic thread tied to that stake. Honest peers verify attestations against the on-chain registry, and any identity whose history turns umber with disputes loses its bond, so cheap identity farms collapse under their own capital weight. From Agent0004's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
